name: NCNPS B.W. Wells Stewardship Fund
summary: Small grants of up to $1,000 for North Carolina organisations managing natural plant communities, installing native plant and pollinator gardens, or running native plant education.

eligibility.rule: Project avoids non-NC-native plants, the same site two years running, irrigation and hardscape
Plants are bought in the Southeast, not from big box stores
Does not seek funding for land purchases
Gardens and restoration sites offer some public access (a fee or tour is fine); land management is exempt

documents: Statement on how the project relates to the NCNPS mission
Itemized budget with justification for non-plant/seed and soil items
Plant/seed list if requesting funds for plantings

calls.label: Applications due 1 September
calls.recurring: Applications must be received by 1 September; applicants are notified by 1 November of each year.

status.quote: All applications must be received by September 1. Notification will be made to applicants by November 1st of each year.

recurring.quote: All applications must be received by September 1. Notification will be made to applicants by November 1st of each year.

applicant_types.quote: Grants are available to organizations, including federal, state, and local agencies, and local community organizations.

geography.quote: management of natural plant communities in North Carolina, e.g., invasive species control, prescribed burns, erosion control

access.quote: Detailed information and instructions for submitting can be found on the application form.

window.quote: All applications must be received by September 1.

effort.quote: All applications must be received by September 1.

eligibility.quote: NCNPS does not fund • the purchase of plants or seeds not native to North Carolina • sourcing plants from big box stores • projects for the same site in two consecutive years • irrigation projects or installation of hardscape
we will not fund plants purchased outside the southeast or from big box stores
No, this fund is not for land purchases.

Free public access to a native garden or restoration area is not required, but some degree of accessibility, be it entrance fee or guided tour, is necessary for funding. This requirement does not apply to land management (prescribed burns, erosion control, etc) of natural communities and ecologically sensitive areas.

after_award.quote: Submit a short description of the project and photo(s) to be published in Native Plant News, the newsletter of the NCNPS, and on the NCNPS website

documents.quote: Project description • Statement on how the project relates to the NCNPS mission
